title: Why a Drone Can Hover Perfectly Still
description: Test fixture for the viral pipeline: a concept clip about how a quadcopter holds a hover using its IMU and a control loop.

beats.text: It is falling. All the time.
beats.vo: That drone is not floating. It is falling, hundreds of times every second.

beats.text: A tiny sensor catches every wobble
points: Four motors speed up or slow down
beats.vo: Inside is a tiny gyro that feels every wobble. A control loop checks it about four hundred times a second and nudges each of the four motors, so every small fall gets caught before you can see it.
Know someone who thinks drones just float? Send this to them.

caption:
That hovering drone is falling hundreds of times a second. 🚁
A gyro feels each tilt and a control loop corrects the four motors about four hundred times a second, so you never see the fall.
What should we explain next: GPS hold or obstacle avoidance?

viral.emotion: awe + identity (I know how it really works)
viral.open_loop: how something that is always falling looks perfectly still
